column1: [🇬🇧] Why is *"Ich bin lernen Deutsch"* wrong for *"I am learning German"*?
column2: German has no `-ing` continuous form; use Präsens: Ich lerne (gerade) Deutsch.
column3: genau A1 A1-02 A1-02-en-01 contrast-en verbs contrast

column2: wer = who · wo = where (W-question word order: Wo wohnst du? Wer ist das?)
column3: genau A1 A1-04 A1-04-en-01 contrast-en questions contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] Translate *"I have lived here for 3 years"* (and name the tense trap).
column2: Ich wohne seit drei Jahren hier. — German uses Präsens with seit, not Perfekt!
column3: genau A2 A2-04 A2-04-en-01 contrast-en time prepositions contrast

column2: English "must not" (prohibition) = nicht dürfen; German "müssen nicht" = don't have to.
column3: genau A2 A2-07 A2-07-en-01 contrast-en modals contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] Can you omit the relative pronoun as in English *"the man I saw yesterday"*?
column2: Never in German: der Mann, den ich gestern gesehen habe.
column3: genau A2 A2-15 A2-15-en-01 contrast-en relative contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] False friend: what does German *"also"* mean, and how do you say English *"also"*?
column2: German also = so / therefore (pos. 1 adverb); English "also" = auch / außerdem.
column3: genau A2 A2-16 A2-16-en-01 contrast-en connectors contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] English uses *"before / after"* before both nouns and clauses. How does German split them?
column2: Before a noun: vor ■ / nach ■ (vor dem Essen, nach der Arbeit); before a clause (V-END): bevor / nachdem (bevor ich esse, nachdem ich gearbeitet hatte).
column3: genau B1 B1-04 B1-04-en-01 contrast-en connectors prepositions contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] English *"If I had time"* uses Simple Past. Why is *"Wenn ich Zeit hatte"* wrong for an unreal condition?
column2: Wenn ich Zeit hatte means "Whenever I had time (in the past, real)". Unreal present needs Konjunktiv II: Wenn ich Zeit hätte.
column3: genau B1 B1-06 B1-06-en-01 contrast-en konjunktiv contrast

column1: [🇬🇧] English *"The shop was closed at 6 pm"* uses *"was"* for both action and state. How does German distinguish them?
column2: Action (someone locked it) = wurde geschlossen; State (it was shut) = war geschlossen.
column3: genau B1 B1-07 B1-07-en-01 contrast-en passiv contrast
